source_ref: Python official documentation plus Formula-90 policy

entries.content: Use pathlib.Path for filesystem operations and resolve the repository/tool root explicitly before depending on relative paths. Path.resolve() is appropriate when symlinks and .. components must be normalized.
For normal one-shot external commands, use subprocess.run() and inspect return code/output explicitly. Set cwd intentionally for repository tools instead of inheriting an unknown working directory.

entries.topic: Prefer argument lists over shell parsing
entries.content: Pass external command arguments as an explicit sequence when possible. Only use shell execution when shell semantics are actually required, because shell quoting and command interpretation add platform and safety complexity.

A normal JSON file represents one JSON document. Do not repeatedly append independent json.dump() outputs to the same file; use an array/object document or JSONL when append-only records are required.
Treat JSON parse failure as a validation error rather than silently defaulting configuration. Catch JSONDecodeError only where the caller can report or recover with a clear source path.

Use a project virtual environment for Python tooling dependencies. Treat it as disposable and reproducible from dependency declarations; do not commit or move the environment directory as project state.

Use argparse for small standard-library CLI tools that need typed/validated arguments, generated usage text and subcommands/options. Keep command contracts explicit so agents can invoke tools deterministically.
Use tempfile high-level context managers for transient work products when possible so cleanup is automatic and cross-platform. Do not create predictable shared-temp filenames manually.
Use module-level logging.getLogger(__name__) and let the application configure handlers/levels. Distinguish machine-readable command output from diagnostic logs so one does not corrupt the other.

Python is support/offline tooling for Formula-90 unless an explicit architecture decision changes that boundary. Do not move latency-sensitive game runtime responsibilities into Python as a convenience workaround.
